title: Microsoft AI Foundry & Bringing Your Own Models and Agents
audience: Developers, AI Practitioners, and Solutions Architects
summary: Deploying, hosting, and connecting custom models and agent backbones in Microsoft AI Foundry, and linking private endpoints to local IDEs.
learningObjectives: Provision and deploy frontier and open-weight models in Microsoft AI Foundry
Connect private Foundry endpoints to local tools and IDEs (VS Code, Cursor, Cline)
Configure agent system prompts, tool interfaces, and security boundaries
Manage token quotas, spend ceilings, and context window limits

requiredSections.title: 1. Navigating the Model Catalog & Deployment Types
requiredSections.guidance: Explain serverless Pay-As-You-Go API endpoints vs. provisioned managed compute for open weights (Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi-4). Contrast latency, throughput, and SLAs with concrete numbers.

requiredSections.title: 2. Connecting Developer Tools to Private Endpoints
requiredSections.guidance: Provide complete TypeScript and cURL examples demonstrating wire-compatible OpenAI authentication against a private Microsoft Foundry endpoint. Show how to configure VS Code / Cursor / Cline base URLs.

requiredSections.title: 3. Constructing Custom Agents & Tool Boundaries
requiredSections.guidance: Detail how to attach tools (code interpreter, web search, custom REST APIs) to Foundry agent backbones while enforcing least privilege and data classification.

requiredSections.title: 4. Token Quotas, Spend Ceilings & Content Safety
requiredSections.guidance: Explain how to configure TPM limits, token rate limit backoff, and Azure AI Content Safety filters to prevent prompt injection and data exfiltration.

handsOnLab.title: Hands-On Lab: Deploy and Connect a Private Foundry Model Endpoint
steps: Step 1: Obtain your Microsoft Foundry endpoint URL and API key.
Step 2: Configure your local environment (.env) with PROJECT42_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL.
Step 3: Run the reference validation script (node scripts/test-foundry-connection.mjs) to verify latency and model identity.
Step 4: Configure an IDE agent (Cursor / VS Code extension) to route requests to the private endpoint.
